mainTopic: Learning from neighboring פסוקים (סמוכים): עשה דוחה לא תעשה from ציצית and כלאים, and why רבי יהודה accepts סמוכים only in ספר דברים
overview: The גמרא finishes its proof that a positive מצוה (עשה) can override a prohibition (לא תעשה). The proof is that the פסוק forbidding שעטנז sits right next to the מצוה of ציצית. רבי אלעזר brings a source from תהלים that we may learn from neighboring פסוקים (סמוכים), and he gives another example about a יבמה whose יבם has boils. רב יוסף adds that even someone who usually rejects סמוכים, like רבי יהודה, accepts them in ספר דברים. The גמרא proves both halves of this. From a ברייתא about stoning a מכשפה, we see that רבי יהודה normally rejects סמוכים. From a משנה about a woman one's father raped or seduced, we see that he does learn from them in ספר דברים. The רבנן disagree with that reading, saying the פסוקים are interrupted. Finally, the גמרא gives two reasons why ספר דברים is different for רבי יהודה: the placement is clearly on purpose (מוכח), or the words are extra (מופנה).

steps.title: Proof from ציצית and שעטנז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה, because the תורה puts the ban on שעטנז right next to the מצוה of ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Do not wear שעטנז,' and right after: 'Make for yourself twisted fringes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the source for its earlier claim that a positive מצוה can push aside a prohibition. It quotes two פסוקים that sit right next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק forbids wearing wool and linen together (שעטנז). The very next פסוק commands ציצית. Putting them side by side teaches that ציצית may be made of wool and linen together, so the עשה of ציצית overrides the לא תעשה of כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment of wool and linen mixed together, which is forbidden to wear
Twisted threads: the fringes of ציצית
A positive מצוה overrides a prohibition
Forbidden mixtures (here, wool and linen)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה, which the whole sugya builds on.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'You shall not wear wool and linen together,'
phrases.notes: This finishes the גמרא's earlier question: how do we know a positive מצוה can push aside a prohibition? דברים 22:11

phrases.english: 'You shall make for yourself twisted fringes.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (from before this section) of how we know an עשה overrides a לא תעשה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The placement of the ציצית פסוק right after the שעטנז פסוק (דברים 22:11-12)

steps.title: Source that neighboring פסוקים teach us
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר shows from תהלים that we may learn laws from פסוקים placed next to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: How do we know from the תורה that we learn from neighboring פסוקים? Because it says: 'They are placed together forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The proof in step 1 depended on two פסוקים being next to each other. Now רבי אלעזר gives the source that this kind of learning (סמוכים) is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the word סמוכים in תהלים as 'placed next to each other.' He takes it to mean that the מצוות were placed side by side on purpose, so their placement teaches something. This backs up the method used in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Neighboring פסוקים; learning a law from the fact that two פסוקים sit side by side
From where do we know?
As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
From where in the Torah do we know to learn from neighboring verses?
As it is said: 'Placed together forever and ever,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 111:8

phrases.english: 'made in truth and uprightness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: סְמוּכִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the method of step 1 by proving that סמוכים is a valid way to learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laws may be learned from the placement of פסוקים next to each other (סמוכים).

steps.title: A יבמה whose יבם has boils
steps.stepSummary: Another example of סמוכים: a יבמה is not forced to marry a יבם with boils, learned from the muzzling פסוק placed next to the יבום section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: How do we know that a יבמה who falls to a יבם with boils may not be 'muzzled'? Because it says, 'Do not muzzle an ox while it threshes,' and right next to it: 'When brothers live together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רבי אלעזר that also uses סמוכים. It shows how he actually applies the method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about not muzzling an ox sits right before the section of יבום. Just as we may not silence the ox, we may not silence the יבמה's complaint when she does not want to marry a יבם with boils (מוכה שחין). So she is not forced into יבום, and he must give חליצה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died childless, who falls to his brother for יבום
A man afflicted with boils (a painful skin disease)
Muzzle; here, silence or force
And right next to it is placed

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said that Rabbi Elazar said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיבָמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לִפְנֵי מוּכֵּה שְׁחִין
phrases.english: From where do we know regarding a yevama who fell before a man afflicted with boils
that we do not muzzle her?
phrases.notes: He means we don't silence her and force her to marry him; instead he has to release her with חליצה.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:4

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'If brothers dwell together.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5, the start of the יבום section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second example of רבי אלעזר using סמוכים, showing the method in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה is not forced into יבום with a יבם who has boils, learned from the muzzling פסוק next to the יבום section.

steps.title: Everyone learns סמוכים in ספר דברים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that even those who usually reject learning from neighboring פסוקים accept it in ספר דברים, as רבי יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Even the one who usually does not learn from neighboring פסוקים does learn from them in ספר דברים. For רבי יהודה usually does not learn from them, but in ספר דברים he does.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why the proofs above work even for those who generally reject סמוכים. Both proofs (ציצית and יבמה) come from ספר דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone accepts סמוכים in general; רבי יהודה is the example of someone who rejects it. But רב יוסף says that in ספר דברים, even רבי יהודה learns from neighboring פסוקים. So the proof of עשה דוחה לא תעשה from ציצית and כלאים, found in ספר דברים, holds for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who does not expound
Generally, everywhere else
ספר דברים
For indeed, as we see

steps.whatToRemember: The ציצית/שעטנז proof for עשה דוחה לא תעשה rests on סמוכים, and since it is in ספר דברים, even someone like רבי יהודה who usually rejects סמוכים would accept it.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying רבי יהודה accepts סמוכים everywhere. He rejects it in general and accepts it only in ספר דברים.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ סְמוּכִים בְּעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: Even according to the one who does not generally expound neighboring verses,
in Mishneh Torah he does expound them.
phrases.notes: משנה תורה here means ספר דברים, where both of our proofs come from.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּעָלְמָא לָא דָּרֵישׁ,
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda generally does not expound them,
yet in Mishneh Torah he does expound them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ סְמוּכִים בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the proofs from סמוכים by showing they apply even for those who usually reject the method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ספר דברים, even those who usually reject סמוכים learn from neighboring פסוקים, as shown by רבי יהודה.

steps.title: How do we know רבי יהודה usually does not learn from neighboring verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the first half of רב יוסף's claim: that רבי יהודה normally rejects סמוכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in general, how do we know that he does not learn from neighboring verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that רבי יהודה normally does not learn from סמוכים. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said רבי יהודה accepts סמוכים only in ספר דברים. That claim has two parts: he rejects it elsewhere, and he accepts it in דברים. The גמרא now asks for proof of the first part.

keyTerms.meaning: In general; everywhere else
From where do we know?
He learns laws from it (from the פסוקים)

phrases.english: And in general, from where do we know that he does not derive [from neighboring verses]?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהודה, from רב יוסף's statement just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the first half of רב יוסף's claim about רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי יהודה generally rejects learning from סמוכים.

steps.title: בן עזאי learns stoning for a sorceress from the neighboring verse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בן עזאי says a מכשפה is stoned, because her פסוק sits next to the פסוק about someone who lies with an animal, and that person is stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: בן עזאי says the תורה says 'Do not let a sorceress live,' and right after that it says 'Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death.' The תורה placed them next to each other to teach: just as one who lies with an animal is stoned, so is a sorceress stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where בן עזאי uses סמוכים to decide how a מכשפה is executed. This prepares for רבי יהודה's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a מכשפה is put to death but does not say how. בן עזאי fills that gap from the very next פסוק, about someone who lies with an animal, whose punishment elsewhere is סקילה. This is a classic use of סמוכים.

keyTerms.meaning: A sorceress; a woman who practices witchcraft
Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
The Torah placed this topic next to that one

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: בן עזאי says,
It is stated: "You shall not let a sorceress live,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:17. Notice it says she dies but not how.

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶאֱמַר: ״כׇּל שׁוֹכֵב עִם בְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת״,
phrases.english: And it is stated: "Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:18, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: [The Torah] placed this topic next to that one, [to teach]:
Just as one who lies with an animal is [punished] by stoning,
phrases.notes: We know he is stoned from ויקרא 20:16.

phrases.english: So too, a sorceress is [punished] by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 5 by quoting the ברייתא in which רבי יהודה will reject סמוכים.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה rejects סמוכים outside ספר דברים (proven by his reply to בן עזאי).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: בן עזאי's derivation of stoning for a מכשפה from שמות 22:17-18.

steps.title: רבי יהודה refuses to stone someone based on neighboring verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה objects: just because two פסוקים are next to each other, should we give someone the death penalty of stoning?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Just because the Torah placed this topic next to that one, should we take this person out to be stoned?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה rejects בן עזאי's proof. This is the proof the גמרא wanted: רבי יהודה does not rely on סמוכים here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not argue about the result, only about the method. For him, two פסוקים simply standing side by side is too weak a basis for something as serious as stoning a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really because...? (a challenging tone)
Shall we take him out to be stoned?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה agrees that a מכשפה is stoned. He only disagrees about WHERE we learn it from.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said to him:
And just because [the Torah] placed this topic next to that one,
shall we take this one out to be stoned?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּמָכוֹ עִנְיָן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה rejects בן עזאי's method of learning from סמוכים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the method (סמוכים) as a source, not the law that a מכשפה is stoned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Neighboring פסוקים are too weak a basis to impose the death penalty of סקילה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own source: a comparison to אוב and ידעוני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says אוב and ידעוני are types of sorcery that the Torah singled out and said are stoned, to teach that every מכשפה is stoned too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the אוב and ידעוני were part of the general group of sorcerers. Why did the תורה single them out? To compare the others to them and teach you: just as an אוב and ידעוני are stoned, so too a sorceress is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different source for stoning a מכשפה, one that does not use סמוכים. This completes the proof that he generally rejects סמוכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אוב and ידעוני are types of sorcery, yet the תורה gave them their own פסוק with stoning. רבי יהודה reads that as a הקש: the rule stated for them applies to all sorcery. He reaches the same result as בן עזאי, but through a method he accepts.

keyTerms.meaning: Two specific types of forbidden sorcery that the תורה names on their own
Included in the general group
Why were they singled out?
To make a הקש, a comparison set up by the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה rejects learning from סמוכים in general, even when he agrees with the law. He prefers a stronger source, such as a הקש.

phrases.english: Rather: the אוב and the ידעוני
were included among sorcerers,
and why were they singled out?
phrases.notes: They get their own פסוק with stoning in ויקרא 20:27.

phrases.english: To compare [others] to them and to tell you:
Just as an אוב and ידעוני are [punished] by stoning,
So too, a sorceress is [punished] by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי בִּכְלַל מְכַשְּׁפִים הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting סמוכים, רבי יהודה gives his own source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מכשפה is stoned, learned from a הקש to אוב and ידעוני and not from סמוכים.

steps.title: How do we know רבי יהודה does learn from neighboring verses in דברים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof of the second half of רב יוסף's claim: that in ספר דברים, רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in משנה תורה, how do we know that he does learn from neighboring verses?
steps.whatsHappening: Having shown that רבי יהודה usually rejects סמוכים, the גמרא now asks for proof that he accepts them in ספר דברים. This sets up the משנה that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of רב יוסף's claim is now proven. This question turns to the second half, the exception for ספר דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for ספר דברים
That he does learn [from neighboring verses]

phrases.english: And in משנה תורה, from where do we know that he does derive?
phrases.notes: משנה תורה here simply means ספר דברים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of רב יוסף's claim to the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that רבי יהודה accepts סמוכים in ספר דברים.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי יהודה forbids a woman his father raped or seduced
steps.stepSummary: A משנה: a man may marry a woman his father or son raped or seduced. רבי יהודה forbids the woman raped or seduced by his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A man may marry a woman his father raped or seduced, and a woman his son raped or seduced. רבי יהודה forbids a woman his father raped or seduced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה adds a prohibition. This sets up the proof, which the גמרא explains right after this: his source will turn out to be סמוכים in ספר דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the ban on a father's wife or son's wife applies only to an actual wife, not to a woman who was raped or seduced. רבי יהודה adds a ban on a woman raped or seduced by the father. The גמרא will show that his source is two neighboring פסוקים in דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was raped
A woman who was seduced
Forbids

steps.confusionAlert: Do not reverse the opinions: the first opinion allows all four cases, and רבי יהודה forbids only the father's cases, not the son's.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: A man may marry a woman raped by his father
and a woman seduced by his father,
a woman raped by his son and a woman seduced by his son.
רבי יהודה forbids
a woman raped by his father and a woman seduced by his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 9 by quoting the משנה whose reasoning will show רבי יהודה using סמוכים in דברים.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in ספר דברים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי יהודה forbids a woman raped or seduced by one's father. Steps 11-13 explain his source.

steps.title: רב explains the source for רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב says that רבי יהודה's source is ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״. This means a woman his father was with is forbidden to the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: What is רבי יהודה's reason? The verse says, "A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt." This means a skirt his father has seen, he may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's explanation of why רבי יהודה forbids a man to marry the woman his father raped or seduced. The source is the phrase ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כנף אביו״ is read as any woman the father was with, even a woman he was never married to. So the woman the father raped is also forbidden to the son. The next question is how we know this פסוק is speaking about a raped woman at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
His father's skirt (garment); here it means a woman the father was with
He shall not uncover, meaning he may not be with her

phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה from step 10: a man can't marry the woman his father raped or seduced.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו
phrases.english: As it is written: "A man shall not take his father's wife
and shall not uncover his father's skirt"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:1

phrases.english: A skirt that his father saw, he shall not uncover.
phrases.notes: In plain words: a woman his father was with is off-limits to the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's source is ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״. A woman the father was with is forbidden to the son.

steps.title: How do we know the verse is about a raped woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that ״כנף אביו״ refers to a woman the father raped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this verse is talking about a woman who was raped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the key point of the proof. Where do we see that the פסוק is about a raped woman?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the words ״כנף אביו״ themselves mentions rape. The answer will have to come from where the פסוק is placed, and that is exactly the סמוכים point the גמרא is trying to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we know)?
A woman who was raped

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is written about a raped woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how step 11's פסוק connects to a raped woman.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that ״לא יגלה כנף אביו״ is speaking about a woman the father raped?

steps.title: From the verse right before it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק just before is about a man who raped a girl and pays her father fifty silver pieces. Our פסוק comes right after it, so it is about that kind of woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the verse above it. That verse says, "And the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty silver pieces," and right next to it comes "A man shall not take, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the link comes from the פסוק right above, which deals with rape. Because the two פסוקים are next to each other, רבי יהודה learns one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה is learning from סמוכים, from two פסוקים placed side by side, and this is in ספר דברים. That answers the question of step 9 and proves the second half of רב יוסף's claim from step 4: in דברים, רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the verse above it
And right next to it
Fifty silver pieces, the fine a man who raped a girl pays her father

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה forbids the woman the father raped because ״כנף אביו״ comes right after the פסוק about rape. This proves he learns from סמוכים in ספר דברים.

phrases.english: From the verse above it,
as it is written: "And the man who lay with her shall give
to the girl's father fifty silver pieces"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

phrases.english: and right next to it: "A man shall not take, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question, and this completes the proof asked for in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק before it is about rape, and ״לא יקח איש...״ is placed right next to it. So רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים here in דברים.

steps.title: The רבנן say the verses are not really next to each other
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that the learning would work if the פסוקים were truly next to each other. But the phrase ״לא יקח איש את אשת אביו״ stands in between and breaks the connection.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say: If it were right next to it, it would be as you say. But now it is not right next to it, because "A man shall not take his father's wife" is written in between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who argue with רבי יהודה, deal with this proof. They reject the connection, and this sets up their own reading of the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that a true סמוך could teach this. But between the rape פסוק and ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״ stand the words ״לא יקח איש את אשת אביו״. Those words interrupt, so ״כנף אביו״ is not really next to the rape פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the majority opinion), who argue with רבי יהודה
As you are saying
Now (that is, as things actually are)
In between

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not saying they never learn from סמוכים. They are saying that here the פסוקים are not truly next to each other.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: How would the רבנן, who allow this woman, answer the proof?

phrases.english: If it were right next to it, it would be as you say.
Now that it is not right next to it

phrases.aramaic: (דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו״ בֵּנְתַיִם) —
phrases.english: (since "A man shall not take his father's wife" is written in between)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The point is that this פסוק sits in between the two parts.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבנן אי הוה סמיך ליה כדקאמרת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the סמוכים connection made in step 13, from the side of the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the use of this סמוך to forbid the woman the father raped.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words ״לא יקח איש את אשת אביו״ stand in between, so ״כנף אביו״ is not truly next to the rape פסוק.

steps.title: The רבנן's reading: the father's שומרת יבם, an extra prohibition
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״ speaks about a woman waiting for the father to do יבום. Someone who is with her breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is speaking about a woman waiting for her יבם, and it comes to make him break two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן explain what ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״ teaches if it is not about a raped woman. It is about a woman waiting for the father to do יבום with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's brother died, and his widow is waiting for the father as her יבם. She is already forbidden to the son as his uncle's wife. This פסוק calls her ״כנף אביו״ and adds a second לאו, so he breaks two prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
The verse is speaking (about)
Two negative commandments

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה reads ״כנף אביו״ as the woman the father raped, learned from סמוכים. The רבנן say the סמוך is interrupted. For them it is the father's שומרת יבם, and it adds a second לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the full disagreement. Both sides use the same פסוק. The question is whether its placement next to the rape פסוק counts.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about a woman waiting for her יבם,
phrases.notes: Here the father is the יבם: his brother died, and the widow is waiting for him.

phrases.english: and it comes to make him break two prohibitions.
phrases.notes: She is already forbidden to the son as his uncle's wife. This פסוק adds a second לאו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's answer from step 14 by giving their own reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different meaning for the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might have thought ״כנף אביו״ must refer to the woman the father raped, because of the rape פסוק before it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן it refers to the father's שומרת יבם, and it adds a second לאו for the son.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה learn from neighboring verses in ספר דברים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה, who usually does not learn from סמוכין, does learn from them in משנה תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in ספר דברים, what is the reason that he does learn from neighboring verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבי יהודה's method. This sets up the next steps, which give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof (steps 11–13) depends on two פסוקים being next to each other. But רבי יהודה normally does not learn from that, except in ספר דברים. The גמרא wants to know what makes ספר דברים different.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the repetition of the תורה': the name for ספר דברים
He learns a law from the text (he expounds it)
Learning a law from the fact that two פסוקים are placed next to each other

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses at all. He usually does not. The question is why ספר דברים is an exception for him.

phrases.english: And in Deuteronomy
phrases.notes: Earlier on this דף, the גמרא said רבי יהודה usually does not learn from neighboring verses, but in ספר דברים he does.

phrases.english: what is the reason that he expounds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific argument with the רבנן to a question about רבי יהודה's general method
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes ספר דברים special, so that רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses there

steps.title: Two possible reasons: it is clear, or it is free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two short answers: either the connection is obvious (מוכח), or the פסוק is extra and free to teach (מופנה).
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because it is evident. And if you want, say it is because it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible answers in short form. The next two steps explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers work in different ways. One says the placement of the פסוק itself shows it is meant to be read with its neighbor. The other says some words are extra, and extra words are free to teach a lesson from their placement.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: a way to offer one of several possible answers
It is evident; the context shows it clearly
Free: words not needed for their plain meaning, so they are open to teach something else

phrases.english: If you wish, say — because it is evident;
and if you wish, say — because it is free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמוֹכַח וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמוּפְנֵי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two options: the connection is evident (מוכח), or the פסוק is extra and free (מופנה)

steps.title: First reason: the verse is out of its natural place
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition of a father's wife belongs with the other forbidden relationships in ויקרא. Since the תורה put it in ספר דברים instead, the placement must be teaching something.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because it is evident. For if it were not meant to teach from its placement, the תורה should have written it together with the other עריות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first answer: the placement of this פסוק is clearly on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden relationships (עריות) are all listed together in ויקרא. A rule about a father's wife would naturally go there. Since the תורה put it in ספר דברים, right after the case of the forced girl, that placement must be meant to teach a lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: a name for ה׳, used when speaking about what the תורה wrote
The forbidden relationships, listed together in ויקרא
For if so: if it were really as you say

phrases.english: If you wish, say because it is evident —
for if so, let the Merciful One write it
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if the placement were not meant to teach anything.

phrases.english: alongside the forbidden relationships.
phrases.notes: That list is in ויקרא 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמוֹכַח דְּאִם כֵּן לִכְתְּבֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי עֲרָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first answer from step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule about a father's wife is out of its natural place (the list of עריות), so its placement is clearly meant to teach

steps.title: Second reason: the extra words are free to teach
steps.stepSummary: ״לא יקח איש את אשת אביו״ already forbids a father's wife, so ״לא יגלה כנף אביו״ is extra. That makes it free to teach a lesson from its placement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is because it is free. For if not, the תורה should have written only ״A man shall not take his father's wife.״ Why do I need ״He shall not uncover his father's skirt״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second answer: part of the פסוק is extra, so it can be used to learn something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק already teaches that a father's wife is forbidden. The second half, ״ולא יגלה כנף אביו״, would add nothing if it meant the same thing. Since it is extra, it is free to teach רבי יהודה's law about a woman the father raped or seduced.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This points out that words seem extra
Literally 'his father's skirt': a woman connected to his father

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns from neighboring verses in ספר דברים for two possible reasons. Either the verse is clearly out of place, so its placement means something (מוכח). Or its words are extra, so they are free to teach (מופנה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: even someone who does not usually learn from neighboring verses will do so when the placement is clearly on purpose or the words are extra.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say because it is free —
for if so, let the Merciful One write:
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if these words were not meant to teach something extra.

phrases.english: "A man shall not take his father's wife";
phrases.notes: דברים 23:1

phrases.english: why do I need "he shall not uncover his father's skirt"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמוּפְנֵי דְּאִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second answer from step 17, offered as another way to answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase ״לא יגלה כנף אביו״ is extra, so it is free to teach through its placement
